Four of the five also had major lower leg malformations, such as tibia or fibular hypoplasia or aplasia. One lower limb had a normal anatomy, including the foot, but all of the lower limbs showed some type of foot deformity. in_text_mentions: She had several stigmata of thalidomide embryopathy. These included strabismus, high-arched palate, and a right external ear that was smaller than the left external ear (Figures 1, 2). She also had absent bones in her wrist, absent digits in her hands and no toes on her feet, shortened tibia and fibula, and hypermobility of her hip (Figures 3, 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Dorsal clinical photograph of both hands of a female patient whose mother had thalidomide exposure during gestation; the caption and in-text history directly attribute the severe upper-extremity limb deficiency to thalidomide embryopathy, and the image visibly shows phocomelic limbs with radial ray/thumb deficiency. B: Palmar clinical photograph of both hands of the same patient; caption and in-text history attribute the findings to thalidomide embryopathy, and the image visibly shows phocomelic upper limbs with radial ray/thumb deficiency.

panels.figure_caption: Thalidomide embryopathy affecting the upper extremities mimics a mutilation injury. The dorsal view (A) and the palmar view (B) of the right and left hand of a female whose mother had been exposed to thalidomide during gestation. The images have not been previously published.
in_text_mentions: A complete skin examination was performed. Inspection revealed severe abnormalities of both the distal upper extremities and lower extremities (Figures 3, 4). This was her first visit to see me, and my initial impression was that the defects were compatible with either a severe injury or mutilating torture. Additional history was obtained; her mother had been exposed to thalidomide during pregnancy.

The image visibly shows a shortened/hypoplastic femur with distal femoral angular deformity, consistent with thalidomide embryopathy long-bone malformation. Blue annotation lines mark the femoral long axis and the measured varus/valgus angle at the distal femur, supporting the captioned measurement context.

Real patient radiology image, not a diagram or control. No configured vocabulary finding applies (no phocomelia, thumb/radial defect, ear, eye or facial anomaly visible), so the finding is recorded as a proposed finding; degenerative disc disease is a recognized non-classic (variant) TE association rather than a textbook congenital sign. Age is not stated in the caption or in-text (title mention of 'middle-aged' is not caption/in-text evidence per rule 10), so age_group is unknown. panels.figure_caption: Thalidomide embryopathy involving the feet mimics injury secondary to severe torture. The frontal (A) and lateral (B) views of the right and left foot show an absence of multiple digits; the female’s mother had been treated with thalidomide during pregnancy. The images have not been previously published.
in_text_mentions: A complete skin examination was performed. Inspection revealed severe abnormalities of both the distal upper extremities and lower extremities (Figures 3, 4). This was her first visit to see me, and my initial impression was that the defects were compatible with either a severe injury or mutilating torture. Additional history was obtained; her mother had been exposed to thalidomide during pregnancy.
